title: On the federal exclusion list, and paid by the City
question: Is any firm on the federal government's exclusion list a City payee, a member of a City contract team, a contractor of another local public body or a bidder?
finding: The federal list holds 35,252 records for firms and other organisations. 5 names on it match a City payee (paid $5,000 or more since fiscal 2019), a contract-team member, another body's contractor or a bidder; 1 match is confirmed by the same street address: Empire Engineering & Construction Inc. (SBA, ineligible (proceedings pending), active 2017-11-06; City paid $7.2 million since fiscal 2019, $7.2 million of it in later fiscal years, 5 contract teams begun afterwards). For the other 4 the records do not show whether the excluded firm and the City payee are the same organisation; most are excluded in another State or country. None of the matches is a contractor of another local body or a bidder on the bid sheets.
how: Records classified as firms or special entities in the public exclusions extract (individuals are not read) are matched by exact normalised name. The address test compares the street address on the exclusion record with every address the Treasurer's business registry and the State contractor-licence file hold for a business of that name.
limits: Federal exclusion applies to federal contracts, grants and federally funded work; it does not by itself bar a City-funded contract. A common trade name can belong to unrelated firms in different States, which is why unconfirmed rows are worded as unknown. The extract is a snapshot; exclusions that ended before it was taken are not in it.
